papers.title: Giant orbital Zeeman effects in a magnetic topological van der Waals interphase
papers.authors: Tobias Wichmann, Mirco Sastges, Keda Jin, Jose Martinez-Castro, Tom G. Saunderson, Dongwook Go, Honey Boban, Samir Lounis, Lukasz Plucinski, Markus Ternes, Yuriy Mokrousov, F. Stefan Tautz, Felix Lüpke
papers.summary_en: Graphene/Fe3GeTe2 interfaces exhibit electrically tunable orbital Zeeman splitting with effective g factors as large as about 230.
papers.summary: Graphene/Fe3GeTe2 interfaces exhibit electrically tunable orbital Zeeman splitting with effective g factors as large as about 230.
papers.abstract: Abstract Van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures allow the engineering of magnetic and electronic properties via interfacial orbital hybridization and charge transfer. The resulting electric fields can give rise to Rashba spin-orbit coupling and Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interactions, which may stabilize novel two-dimensional magnetic phases. While such emergent magnetic ‘interphases’ may offer a promising platform for spin-based electronics, direct spectroscopic evidence for them is still lacking. Here, we report electric-field tunable Zeeman effects with Landé g -factors up to ≈ 230 at the interface of graphene and the vdW ferromagnet Fe 3 GeTe 2 . They arise from an interplay of local-moment canting and the itinerant orbital moments of Fe 3 GeTe 2 , producing a giant asymmetric level splitting. Exploiting the inelastic phonon gap of graphene, scanning tunneling spectroscopy allows us to access the buried interface properties, and quantify Faraday-like screening. Our findings provide new insights and opportunities for electrically controlled interface magnetism, e.g. for spintronics and orbitronics devices.
papers.summary_zh: 在石墨烯/Fe₃GeTe₂ 界面观察到最高约 230 的轨道 Zeeman 有效 g 因子，并用局域电场调节能级分裂。
papers.method_en: Graphene/Fe3GeTe2/graphite van der Waals stack; low-temperature STM/STS near 6 K, perpendicular magnetic field to 3 T, tip-height electrostatic gating, DFT/Wannier orbital-moment calculations.
papers.method_zh: 制备石墨烯/Fe₃GeTe₂/石墨异质结构；在约 6 K 下进行 STM/STS、最高 3 T 面外磁场和针尖高度调控的局域电场实验，并结合 DFT/Wannier 轨道磁矩计算。
papers.result_en: Fig. 1 connects topological band extrema at K/K′ to band orbital moments and interfacial spin canting. Fig. 2 exploits graphene’s ~65 meV inelastic phonon gap to spectroscopically access the buried FGT states. Fig. 3 tracks two interface peaks with field: slopes 1.8 ± 0.3 and 13.3 ± 0.4 meV/T, corresponding to g ≈ 30 and 230. Fig. 4 changes tip–sample distance at fixed B = 2 T and demonstrates electric-field-dependent level shifts. The authors associate the giant splitting with coupled band-orbital and chirality-induced orbital moments.
papers.result_zh: Fig. 1 将 K/K′ 附近拓扑能带极值的轨道磁矩与界面自旋倾斜联系起来；Fig. 2 利用石墨烯约 65 meV 的非弹性声子隧穿间隙读取下方 FGT 态；Fig. 3 的两个峰随磁场移动，斜率分别为 1.8±0.3 与 13.3±0.4 meV/T，对应 g≈30 与 230；Fig. 4 在 B=2 T 固定时改变针尖距离，展示电场调控的能级移动。作者将巨大的分裂归因于能带轨道磁矩与自旋手性轨道磁矩的耦合。
papers.future_en: Measure gate-dependent anomalous Hall and planar/thermal Hall transport on graphene/FGT; compare field-angle hysteresis and electrostatic control to separate local-moment canting from orbital-moment contributions.
papers.future_zh: 可在石墨烯/FGT 器件上做栅压依赖的反常霍尔、面内/热霍尔输运；比较磁场角度、磁滞和电场响应，区分局域自旋倾斜与轨道磁矩贡献。

papers.title: Piezo-Kerr effect in altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets
papers.authors: Yuqi Liu, Qiu-Shi Huang, Xinfeng Chen, Yilin Han, Run-Wu Zhang, Zhi-Ming Yu, Yugui Yao
papers.summary_en: Strain activates symmetry-forbidden Kerr rotation in 16 of 122 magnetic point groups, with calculated signals of tens to hundreds of millidegrees.
papers.summary: Strain activates symmetry-forbidden Kerr rotation in 16 of 122 magnetic point groups, with calculated signals of tens to hundreds of millidegrees.
papers.abstract: Symmetry is usually viewed as a constraint on physical responses, but it can also be used to design the fields that control them. Here, we adopt the representation-matching principle used to identify conjugate fields of order parameters and apply it to response tensors. A linear coupling, the key ingredient for sign-switching control, is symmetry-allowed when a component (or a combination of components) of the control field and the selected response component share the same irreducible representation of the magnetic point group (MPG) of the system. Applied to the magneto-optical Kerr effect, this principle yields a piezo-Kerr effect, in which specific strain combinations activate a Kerr response forbidden in the unstrained state. Enumerating all 122 MPGs, we identify 16 groups in which the unstrained Kerr response is forbidden while a linear strain-induced contribution is allowed. These groups are realized by altermagnets and noncollinear antiferromagnets with symmetry-enforced vanishing net magnetization. The active strain channels and the associated first-order sign reversals follow directly from symmetry. First-principles calculations for bulk MnTe$_{2}$ and CoF$_{2}$, and Cr$_{2}$Se$_{2}$O and Cr$_{2}$Te$_{2}$O monolayers confirm these predictions. In these materials, the Kerr rotation vanishes without strain, whereas 0.5-3% strain produces rotations ranging from tens to hundreds of millidegrees, and reversing the matched strain channel reverses the Kerr sign. These results establish a general route to large and switchable Kerr responses emerging from symmetry-forbidden states in compensated magnets.
papers.summary_zh: 提出应变激活原本对称性禁戒的 Kerr 响应；122 种磁点群中有 16 种允许线性效应，预测 Kerr 旋转可达数十至数百毫度。
papers.tier_reason_en: A general symmetry selection rule with quantitative material predictions and a clean, testable sign-reversal signature.
papers.tier_reason_zh: 普适对称性选择定则、定量材料预测及干净可检验的符号翻转特征，具备 PRL 水平潜力。
papers.method_en: Magnetic-point-group representation analysis over all 122 MPGs, followed by first-principles magneto-optical conductivity and strain calculations for bulk MnTe2, CoF2 and monolayer Cr2Se2O/Cr2Te2O.
papers.method_zh: 枚举全部 122 种磁点群的表示，计算线性应变–Kerr 张量；随后对块体 MnTe₂、CoF₂ 及单层 Cr₂Se₂O/Cr₂Te₂O 做第一性原理应变与磁光电导计算。
papers.result_en: The central equation is θ_i = Σ_jk Λ_i,jk ε_jk, where the time-reversal-odd piezo-Kerr tensor Λ is symmetry-constrained. Fig. 1 illustrates a zero-background Kerr signal activated and sign-reversed by strain. Table 1 identifies 16 MPGs allowing the response; for 4′/mm′m, θ_z ∝ ε_xx−ε_yy. The calculated Cr2Se2O response (Fig. 4) reaches ~50 mdeg at 1% and 164 mdeg at 3% strain (photon energy 1.44 eV). The authors extend representation matching from order parameters to response tensors.
papers.result_zh: 核心公式为 θ_i=Σ_jk Λ_i,jk ε_jk，其中时间反演奇的 piezo-Kerr 张量 Λ 由磁点群对称性约束。Fig. 1 展示零背景 Kerr 信号被应变激活并随应变反向翻转；Table 1 列出允许该响应的 16 种磁点群，例如 4′/mm′m 中 θ_z∝ε_xx−ε_yy；Fig. 4 计算单层 Cr₂Se₂O 在 1% 应变下约 50 mdeg、3% 下约 164 mdeg（光子能量 1.44 eV）。作者将序参量的表示匹配原则推广到响应张量。
papers.future_en: Test bulk CoF2 or MnTe2 with piezo-driven AC strain and lock-in Kerr rotation; use orthogonal εxx−εyy channels and magnetic-domain training to verify linearity and sign reversal before seeking transverse transport analogues.
papers.future_zh: 优先在块体 CoF₂ 或 MnTe₂ 上施加压电 AC 应变，用锁相 Kerr 测量；对比 εxx−εyy 的正负通道并训练磁畴，验证线性关系与符号翻转，再寻找相应横向输运响应。

papers.title: Anisotropic thermoelectric transport in the Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system
papers.authors: Takeru Ito, Shogo Yoshida, Hiroshi Yaguchi, Ryuji Okazaki
papers.summary_en: Thermopower measured parallel and perpendicular to Ru lamellae in Sr2RuO4–Ru eutectics is anisotropic; local strain modeling captures its sign and approximate magnitude.
papers.summary: Thermopower measured parallel and perpendicular to Ru lamellae in Sr2RuO4–Ru eutectics is anisotropic; local strain modeling captures its sign and approximate magnitude.
papers.abstract: The Sr2RuO4-Ru eutectic system, in which metallic Ru inclusions are embedded in a Sr2RuO4 matrix, exhibits an enhanced superconducting onset temperature of about 3 K, known as the 3-K phase. Here we investigate the in-plane thermoelectric response of this eutectic system in the normal state and find a pronounced anisotropy in the thermopower for thermal gradients applied parallel and perpendicular to the Ru lamellae. To clarify its origin, we combine thermopower measurements with electronic-structure-based transport calculations and finite-element modeling of the local strain distribution generated by the thermal-expansion mismatch between Sr2RuO4 and Ru. The calculations show that uniaxial compression of Sr2RuO4 produces a sizable thermopower anisotropy through modification of the Fermi surfaces. When an idealized spatially inhomogeneous strain field around the Ru lamellae is included, the observed sign and qualitative magnitude of the anisotropy are reproduced more closely than in a simple unstrained two-component model. These results are consistent with a substantial contribution from strain-induced changes in the Sr2RuO4 electronic structure near the interfaces, although contributions from interfacial phase mixing and three-dimensional transport connectivity cannot be excluded.
papers.summary_zh: 在 Sr₂RuO₄–Ru 共晶中测得相对 Ru 片层平行与垂直方向的热电势各向异性，局域应变模型解释其符号和量级。
papers.tier_reason_en: Careful Seebeck and strain-model comparison; its central interpretation is qualitative and based on one eutectic sample.
papers.tier_reason_zh: Seebeck 与应变模拟结合较完整，但目前主要是单块共晶样品上的定性机制论证。
papers.method_en: Floating-zone-grown Sr2RuO4–Ru eutectic with ~2% visible Ru lamellae; steady-state Seebeck measurements for heat gradients parallel/perpendicular to lamellae; DFT Boltzmann transport and finite-element strain maps.
papers.method_zh: 使用浮区法生长的 Sr₂RuO₄–Ru 共晶（表面 Ru 片层面积约 2%）；沿片层平行/垂直方向测稳态 Seebeck 系数，结合 DFT Boltzmann 输运和有限元局域应变模拟。
papers.result_en: Fig. 1 compares Sxx and Syy of the eutectic with a pure Sr2RuO4 reference and establishes anisotropy tied to lamellar orientation. Figs. 2–3 examine uniaxial-strain-driven Fermi-surface changes and the spatial strain distribution near Ru. Fig. 4 shows that an unstrained two-component mixing model produces <1% anisotropy, while a finite-element strain-informed calculation gives the observed sign and a closer magnitude. The authors argue that thermopower is a sensitive normal-state probe of interfacial strain associated with the 3-K superconducting phase.
papers.result_zh: Fig. 1 比较共晶沿 Ru 片层垂直和平行方向的 Sxx、Syy，并以纯 Sr₂RuO₄ 为参照；Figs. 2–3 研究单轴应变导致的费米面变化和 Ru 附近的空间应变分布；Fig. 4 表明简单无应变双组分混合模型只给出小于 1% 的各向异性，而纳入有限元应变后可重现实验符号并更接近量级。作者认为热电势是与 3-K 界面超导有关的局域应变的灵敏常态探针。
papers.future_en: On strain-controlled Sr2RuO4, measure Sxx−Syy and elastocaloric response on the same crystal while tracking Tc and the van-Hove-sensitive thermopower; repeat with several eutectic lamellar orientations.
papers.future_zh: 可在同一块受控应变 Sr₂RuO₄ 样品上同时追踪 Sxx−Syy、弹热响应、Tc 及 van Hove 敏感的热电势；再比较不同 Ru 片层取向的共晶样品。

papers.title: Intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a 2D Ruddlesden-Popper perovskite
papers.authors: Koushik Mondal, Amit Haldar, Indrajit Mondal, Arpita Dutta, Himanshu Bhatt, Biswajit Mahata, Soumili Banerjee, Hirendra Nath Ghosh, Satyaprasad P Senanayak, Shovon Pal
papers.summary_en: The study reports an intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a two-dimensional Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite.
papers.summary: The study reports an intensity-driven Mott-like transition in a two-dimensional Ruddlesden–Popper perovskite.
papers.abstract: Two-dimensional Ruddlesden-Popper-type halide perovskites have emerged as promising cutting-edge nonlinear optical materials due to their strong excitonic effects and carrier-density-dependent optical responses. In this work, we investigate the nonlinear optical properties and ultrafast carrier dynamics of (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ under infrared excitation, resonant with the two-photon energy of its excitonic transition. Using a nonlinear femtosecond Z-scan measurement with a 1030\,nm pump pulse, we observe a pronounced intensity-dependent evolution of the nonlinear absorption coefficient and the refractive index. With increasing pump intensity, a switch from saturable absorption to reverse saturable absorption emerges, suggesting an intensity-driven Mott-like transition. To elucidate the underlying carrier dynamics, intensity-dependent transient absorption spectroscopy was performed under the same excitation intensities. This reveals a long-lived charge carrier population above the estimated Mott density, reflecting a clear phase transition from an exciton-dominated regime to a dense electron-hole plasma regime. Moreover, such an intensity-driven, high, and switchable nonlinear optical response, along with a Mott-like transition under infrared pulse excitation, makes the 2D (BA)$_2$PbI$_4$ perovskites suitable for all-optical operation in the infrared regime.

papers.title: Chiral Cavity Vacua as Local Generators and Probes of Non-Abelian Kitaev Topology
papers.authors: Yu Zhang
papers.summary_en: A chiral cavity vacuum is predicted to write and probe local non-Abelian Kitaev topological regions.
papers.summary: A chiral cavity vacuum is predicted to write and probe local non-Abelian Kitaev topological regions.
papers.abstract: We show how a gyrotropic cavity vacuum generates, probes, and spatially programs non-Abelian topology in the Kitaev honeycomb model. Gauge-consistent virtual-photon elimination produces a universal helicity-odd interaction $\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]$ alongside same-order even dressing. For the leading bond polarization, this commutator is exactly the Kitaev three-spin mass. Mode normalization imposes a thermodynamic constraint: one extended normalized mode gives a local mass that vanishes with sample area, whereas a localized mode writes a finite topological island and a finite mode density enables a bulk mass. The exact Majorana solution yields helicity-reversed Chern gaps and edge propagation, while integrated circular dichroism exactly measures the mass generator, $\langle\mathrm{i}[P_x,P_y]\rangle=-\sqrt3p^2\langle O_3\rangle$. Real-space calculations reveal a non-Abelian island and a helicity wall with two co-propagating Majorana modes. Uniform helicity reversal is a Dirac-mass quench with $n_{\rm ex}\proptoτ_Q^{-1}$, whereas moving a wall localizes the gap closing. The equilibrium vacuum kernel contains sum-frequency rather than resonant denominators. These results establish distinct criteria for local and bulk cavity-induced topology.
papers.summary_zh: 提出用手性腔真空在 Kitaev 蜂窝模型中局域产生、探测和编程非阿贝尔拓扑态。

papers.title: Emergent altermagnetism in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices from interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts
papers.authors: Gustavo H. Cassemiro, Walber H. Brito
papers.summary_en: First-principles calculations predict interfacial-charge-transfer- and octahedral-tilt-induced altermagnetism in LaVO3/LaNiO3 superlattices.
papers.summary: First-principles calculations predict interfacial-charge-transfer- and octahedral-tilt-induced altermagnetism in LaVO3/LaNiO3 superlattices.
papers.abstract: Using first-principles calculations, we show that altermagnetism emerges in (LaVO$_3$)$_n$/(LaNiO$_3$)$_m$ superlattices, with $(n,m) = (1,1), (2,2)$ and $(2,4)$, from the interplay of interfacial charge transfer and octahedral tilts. Charge transfer drives the system towards the V$^{4+}$ and Ni$^{2+}$ configuration, turning the otherwise paramagnetic nickelate layers into a magnetically active sublattice. The resulting $C$-type antiferromagnetic order, combined with $a^-b^+c^-$ or $a^-b^-c^-$ octahedral tilts, links opposite-spin sublattices only through nonsymmorphic operations, yielding a $d$-wave spin splitting without spin-orbit coupling. Within DFT+U, the splitting reaches 118 meV in the insulating (LVO)$_1$/(LNO)$_1$ superlattice, about twice that calculated for bulk LaVO$_3$, and decreases as the nickelate layers become thicker. Our findings indicate that this splitting is hosted by both the V and Ni sublattices, with nearly half of its weight on oxygen $2p$ states through $p$-$d$ covalency. Interfacial charge transfer thus emerges as a \textit{design} principle for engineering altermagnetism in oxide heterostructures.

papers.title: Impact of localized $4f$ magnetism on Berry curvature and the intrinsic anomalous Hall effect in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$
papers.authors: Takehiro Kobayashi, Shunsuke Hirai, Ibuki Terada, Michi-To Suzuki
papers.summary_en: Localized Ce 4f magnetism can induce conduction-band exchange splitting and intrinsic Berry-curvature Hall response in CeRu2Si2.
papers.summary: Localized Ce 4f magnetism can induce conduction-band exchange splitting and intrinsic Berry-curvature Hall response in CeRu2Si2.
papers.abstract: The intrinsic anomalous Hall effect (AHE), originating from Berry curvature, has been extensively studied in $f$-electron systems, including Ce-based compounds. However, how the magnetism of localized $f$ electrons affect the intrinsic AHE remains unclear. Here, we investigate this issue in CeRu$_2$Si$_2$ by calculating the intrinsic anomalous Hall conductivity (AHC) for several occupied Ce-$4f$ states using first-principles LDA+$U$ calculations combined with Wannier interpolation method. We find that the intrinsic AHC remains finite even when the Ce-$4f$ states are localized and do not contribute directly to the Fermi surface, and that its magnitude depends on which Ce-$4f$ state is occupied. We show that localized $4f$-electron magnetism induces exchange splitting in the conduction bands, generating Berry curvature in specific regions near the Fermi surface. This mechanism enables conduction bands that are derived from nonmagnetic orbitals and form the Fermi surface to contribute to the intrinsic AHE, suggesting a route to realizing large intrinsic AHE in $f$-electron materials.

papers.title: Interaction-enhanced antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure
papers.authors: Tatsuya Kaneko, Ritsuki Hirabayashi, Yutaka Akagi
papers.summary_en: Interactions enhance antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure.
papers.summary: Interactions enhance antiferromagnetic correlations in a Kondo ladder with a gapped band structure.
papers.abstract: We investigate magnetic correlations in the two-leg Kondo-Hubbard ladder using the density-matrix renormalization group method. We focus on a parameter regime in which the noninteracting electronic system has a narrow indirect band gap. In this regime, there is no Fermi surface, and the conventional Fermi-surface-based Ruderman-Kittel-Kasuya-Yosida picture is not directly applicable; magnetic correlations between localized spins become weaker as the noninteracting band gap increases. We find that a moderate on-site Coulomb interaction enhances the antiferromagnetic correlations between localized spins. This enhancement, which is also seen in the staggered magnetization induced by a pinning field at the edges, occurs for both ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic Kondo couplings. Our results show that electron-electron interactions can enhance magnetic correlations between localized spins even when the underlying noninteracting electronic structure is gapped, suggesting an interaction-driven route to magnetic instabilities in narrow-gap Kondo-lattice systems.

papers.title: Mn-deficient Ni-Mn-Ga alloys: phase transitions, magnetic properties, and disappearance of martensitic transformation
papers.authors: Valentina Moskvina, Jaroslav Čapek, Michal Rameš, Denys Musiienko, Petr Veřtát, Alexej Perevertov, Ladislav Straka, Oleg Heczko
papers.summary_en: Composition-gradient zone-remelted Ni–Mn–Ga crystals identify a Mn-poor regime where martensitic transformations disappear.
papers.summary: Composition-gradient zone-remelted Ni–Mn–Ga crystals identify a Mn-poor regime where martensitic transformations disappear.
papers.abstract: Composition gradients formed during directional solidification are generally considered undesirable in Ni-Mn-Ga magnetic shape-memory alloys. However, these gradients offer a highly effective platform for systematically investigating composition-property relationships under identical growth and heat-treatment conditions. To exploit this approach, one Mn-deficient and two near-stoichiometric Ni-Mn-Ga oligocrystals were grown by optical zone remelting and characterized by X-ray fluorescence mapping, optical microscopy, X-ray diffraction, low-field magnetic measurements, and vibrating-sample magnetometry. The ingots contained elongated grains and axial compositional gradients, primarily associated with the redistribution of Mn and Ga, whereas Ni remained relatively uniformly distributed. The martensitic and premartensitic transformation temperatures generally increased with increasing Mn content. Neither transformation was detected between 10 and 400 K in specimens containing 20.5-22.0 at.% Mn, all of which had $e/a < 7.40$. In contrast, both transformations were observed in the investigated specimens containing at least 22.1 at.% ($e/a \geq 7.46$). This abrupt change may indicate a possible electron-concentration threshold for the occurrence of these transformations. Saturation magnetization increased with Mn content up to 25.8 at.%, reaching 96.9 A m$^2$/kg at 10 K and 71.2 A m$^2$/kg at 300 K. Post-growth annealing increased the transition temperatures and changed the low-field magnetic response. The results indicate that composition-gradient oligocrystals serve as an effective platform for investigating the relationships between composition, structure, and magnetic properties in Ni-Mn-Ga alloys with the same processing history.

papers.title: Anomalous polar chains in halide perovskites
papers.authors: Erik Fransson, Apinya Ngoipala, Priyanka Deswal, Ethan Berger, Nicholas C. Bristowe, Paul Erhart, Julia Wiktor
papers.summary_en: Molecular dynamics identifies tens-of-nanometers-long, nanosecond-lived polar chains in nominally cubic CsGeBr3.
papers.summary: Molecular dynamics identifies tens-of-nanometers-long, nanosecond-lived polar chains in nominally cubic CsGeBr3.
papers.abstract: Local polar distortions, their collective ordering, and their field-driven reversal have been studied extensively in ferroelectric perovskites for decades. Here we identify an unusual behavior in the ferroelectric halide perovskite CsGeBr3 using large-scale molecular dynamics with first-principles-trained interatomic potentials. In its nominally cubic phase the Ge off-centering forms one-dimensional polar chains that extend over at least tens of nanometers and relax on nanosecond timescales, four orders of magnitude slower than in BaTiO3 and PbTiO3, with CsSnBr3 in between. The cubic CsGeBr3 phase is a dynamically disordered state in which oppositely polarized chains flip throughout the crystal, and a long-lived one-dimensional local polarization coexists with zero net polarization. A simple three-dimensional perovskite thus hosts long-ranged one-dimensional polar correlations with remarkably slow dynamics. In the ferroelectric phase the same chains set a one-dimensional switching mechanism, in which the polarization reverses chain by chain.

papers.title: Chiroptical Valleytronic in SnSe
papers.authors: Yiming Pan, Sotirios Fragkos, Umberto Dellasette, Quentin Courtade, Dominique Descamps, Stéphane Petit, Fabio Caruso, Samuel Beaulieu
papers.summary_en: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission reveals helicity-selective valley excitation and sub-picosecond relaxation in SnSe.
papers.summary: Time- and angle-resolved photoemission reveals helicity-selective valley excitation and sub-picosecond relaxation in SnSe.
papers.abstract: Quantum geometric properties of Bloch electrons play a central role in governing light-matter interactions and transport phenomena in solids. Here, we report quantum-geometric chiroptical selection rules that generate a helicity-dependent momentum-space population imbalance in the group-IV monochalcogenide SnSe. By combining time- and angle-resolved extreme-ultraviolet photoemission spectroscopy with ab initio real-time simulations of photoexcited carrier dynamics, we identify valley-selective excitation at opposite crystal momenta arising from the breaking of time-reversal symmetry under circularly polarized illumination. We theoretically demonstrate that the magnitude of valley circular dichroism is strongly constrained by crystal symmetry through its influence on the quantum geometric tensor, the key quantity underlying valley optical selection rules. The resulting chiroptically induced valley polarization decays on sub-picosecond timescales through intervalley scattering mediated by electron-phonon coupling. Furthermore, we show theoretically that the population imbalance between valleys at opposite momenta gives rise to a helicity-reversible transient photocurrent. These findings provide microscopic insight into how quantum geometry governs valley-selective light-matter interactions, valley polarization, and photocurrent generation in van der Waals materials exhibiting hidden and transient symmetry breaking.

papers.title: Role of Chalcogen-p States in the Optical Response of Bulk PtSe2 and PtTe2
papers.authors: Ji Eun Lee, R. Mathew Roy, Premakumar Yanda, Chandra Shekhar, Claudia Felser, Martin Dressel
papers.summary_en: Optical measurements assess the contribution of chalcogen p states in bulk PtSe2 and PtTe2.
papers.summary: Optical measurements assess the contribution of chalcogen p states in bulk PtSe2 and PtTe2.
papers.abstract: The type-II Dirac semimetals PtSe$_2$ and PtTe$_2$ are isostructural and isovalent layered compounds but exhibit distinct electronic properties. We measure the in-plane infrared reflectivity of bulk crystals between 10 and 300 K and compare the interband contribution to the optical conductivity with band-resolved density-functional calculations. At low temperature, the Drude spectral weight of PtTe$_2$ is an order of magnitude larger than that of PtSe$_2$. PtTe$_2$ also shows a broad mid-infrared absorption continuum, whereas the absorption of PtSe$_2$ remains weak. The calculations attribute this continuum to transitions from a predominantly chalcogen-$p$ band into a Pt-$d$ band. In PtTe$_2$, the chalcogen-$p$ band lies higher in energy, which lowers the onset of these transitions and increases the semimetallic band overlap, in line with the larger Drude spectral weight. The type-II Dirac points lie far below the Fermi level, so that transitions between the bands forming the Dirac cones do not contribute appreciably to the interband conductivity.

papers.title: Coulomb-Driven Electronic Textures in Lightly Hole-Doped Cuprates
papers.authors: Wei-Wei Yang, Yang Shen, Yuxin Wang, Pengfei Li, Mingpu Qin, Kun Jiang
papers.summary_en: Poorly screened Coulomb interactions organize electronic textures in lightly hole-doped cuprates.
papers.summary: Poorly screened Coulomb interactions organize electronic textures in lightly hole-doped cuprates.
papers.abstract: Motivated by recent experiments on Ca$_2$CuO$_2$Cl$_2$, we present a comprehensive study of the interplay between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets in lightly hole-doped cuprates. Owing to the poorly screened Coulomb potential, the interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets favor asymmetric electronic configurations characterized by effective electric "dipoles". Using the MPS-based Lanczos method, we show that these localized holes give rise to in-gap bound states within the charge-transfer gap. When tunneling matrix-element effects are included, the bound states exhibit a characteristic $4a_0 \times 2a_0$ internal structure, consistent with experimental observations. Our results suggest that Coulomb interactions between dopants and localized Zhang-Rice singlets, together with tunneling matrix-element effects, provide a microscopic mechanism for the observed $4a_0$ electronic structures.

papers.title: Extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity in the hole-doped Hubbard model
papers.authors: Ao Chen, Johnnie Gray, Si-Jing Du, Garnet Kin-Lic Chan
papers.summary_en: High-accuracy simulations on up to 1024 sites find near-degenerate uniform d-wave superconducting, superconducting-stripe and insulating-stripe states in the doped Hubbard model.
papers.summary: High-accuracy simulations on up to 1024 sites find near-degenerate uniform d-wave superconducting, superconducting-stripe and insulating-stripe states in the doped Hubbard model.
papers.abstract: The two-dimensional Hubbard model was originally proposed as the minimal model of uniform $d$-wave superconductivity in the cuprate high-temperature superconductors, but recent calculations with relevant parameters in a realistic doping regime have often found other ground states. Further, uncertainty remains over such results due to the intrinsic bias of different computational methods. Here we address this uncertainty through state-of-the-art neural tensor network and neural backflow state simulations, enabled by large-scale GPU computation, that together reach an unprecedented variational accuracy on lattices with up to 1024 sites. At $1/8$ doping in the pure Hubbard model, as well as with next-nearest-neighbor hopping relevant to the hole-doped cuprates, we reveal a near degeneracy among a low-energy uniform $d$-wave state, superconducting stripes, and non-superconducting stripe states on the milli-$t$ energy scale. Our work rebalances the narrative that the Hubbard model supports a single dominant order in relevant parameter regimes towards a picture of extreme competition between stripes and superconductivity.

papers.title: Field-free superconducting diode and tunable vortex dynamics in NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures
papers.authors: Juan C. Zapata, Emilio De Biasi, Martin Sirena, Jeehoon Kim, Nestor Haberkorn
papers.summary_en: NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures exhibit a field-free superconducting diode efficiency of roughly 50–60%, retaining 35–40% with an AlN spacer.
papers.summary: NbN/FePt stripe-domain heterostructures exhibit a field-free superconducting diode efficiency of roughly 50–60%, retaining 35–40% with an AlN spacer.
papers.abstract: We demonstrate reconfigurable, field-free superconducting diode behavior in NbN/FePt and NbN/AlN/FePt heterostructures with remanent stripe domains in the FePt layer. NbN films 10 nm thick are capped either directly with FePt or through a thin AlN spacer, which reduces electronic proximity effects while preserving magnetic coupling through stray fields. At zero applied magnetic field, the superconducting diode efficiency reaches approximately 50--60% in NbN/FePt when the stripes are perpendicular to the current and is strongly reduced when they are parallel. The diode effect persists in NbN/AlN/FePt with efficiencies reaching approximately 35--40%, supporting a magnetic origin of the nonreciprocity. We interpret the response as asymmetric vortex transport in the remanent magnetic landscape, with preferential edge vorticity and a Lorentz force that favors inward flux injection or outward motion depending on current polarity. Under applied perpendicular magnetic fields, the interplay between the external field and the magnetic stray fields modifies the flux-flow instability and the apparent instability velocity inferred from transport, with values below those reported for bare NbN films. These results show that stripe-domain ferromagnetic overlayers provide a reconfigurable route to control superconducting nonreciprocity and flux-flow stability in NbN-based heterostructures.

papers.title: Realization of a Superleak in a Quantum Gas
papers.authors: Wan-Ling Yang, Shao-Bo Liu, Xiang Luo, Chao Yang, Hai-Lin Li, Yu-Zhou Yang, Yong-Kui Wang, Bing Yang
papers.summary_en: An optical superlattice acts as a superleak for atomic gases, giving a superfluid-to-normal flow contrast of 500(49).
papers.summary: An optical superlattice acts as a superleak for atomic gases, giving a superfluid-to-normal flow contrast of 500(49).
papers.abstract: Ultracold quantum gases offer a controllable and microscopically accessible platform for understanding and engineering superfluidity. Yet, realizing a superleak that selectively transports the superfluid while suppressing normal flow has remained elusive. Here, we harness an optical superlattice to realize such a superleak through dynamical selectivity. The superfluid undergoes coherent Josephson transport, whereas the normal component exhibits slow, thermodynamically limited response, resulting in a flow-rate contrast of 500(49). Exploiting this contrast, we demonstrate repeated filtering of the normal component and dynamical purification of the superfluid, while sustaining coherent driven oscillations for up to 100 cycles. Our results establish a controllable atomic superleak and open possibilities for manipulating transport and thermodynamics in quantum fluids.

papers.title: Superheating field of clean superconductors near the type-I--type-II boundary: the low-temperature Meissner stability limit of niobium
papers.authors: Takayuki Kubo
papers.summary_en: The work calculates the low-temperature superheating field and Meissner stability near the type-I/type-II boundary.
papers.summary: The work calculates the low-temperature superheating field and Meissner stability near the type-I/type-II boundary.
papers.abstract: We calculate the low-temperature superheating field $B_{\rm sh}$ of clean superconductors near the boundary between type-I and type-II superconductivity, with particular emphasis on Nb. Ginzburg--Landau theory is not applicable at low temperatures, while previous microscopic calculations have been limited to either the large-$κ$ regime or the dirty limit. The clean, low-$κ$ regime relevant to Nb has therefore remained unresolved. We solve the self-consistent nonlinear nonlocal Eilenberger problem for the Meissner state and then analyze its stability against small perturbations. For a Nb-like material with $κ_{\rm GL}=0.7$, we obtain $B_{\rm sh}\simeq 290\,{\rm mT}$ at $T/T_c=0.2$, using $B_{c0}\simeq 200\,{\rm mT}$. For a TESLA-shaped Nb accelerator cavity, this corresponds to an intrinsic Meissner-stability limit of about $67\,{\rm MV/m}$.

papers.title: Ferroelastic Reversal Magnon Thermal Hall Effect in a Fully Compensated Ferrimagnet
papers.authors: Yingxi Bai, Zihan Chen, Chengwang Niu, Ming Yang
papers.summary_en: Ferroelastic switching is predicted to reversibly control magnon thermal Hall response in fully compensated ferrimagnets.
papers.summary: Ferroelastic switching is predicted to reversibly control magnon thermal Hall response in fully compensated ferrimagnets.
papers.abstract: Magnons offer a charge-neutral channel for spin and heat transport, yet reversible and nonvolatile control of their thermal Hall response poses a fundamental challenge in systems with zero net magnetization. Here, we establish ferroelastic switching as an effective route to manipulate magnonic transverse responses in fully compensated ferrimagnets. A minimal Heisenberg-Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya model reveals that ferroelastic switching can re-orientate the lattice anisotropy, which reconstructs the chirality-resolved magnon bands and Berry curvature distribution. Consequently, the two orthogonal fully compensated ferrimagnetic variants related by [C2||C4z] exhibit magnon thermal Hall responses with opposite signs, whereas the response vanishes in the intermediate altermagnetic phase. First-principles calculations further identify monolayer V2SSe as a promising material candidate for realizing the proposed ferroelastic control of transverse magnon transport. Remarkably, ferroelastic switching drives a dual magnonic-electronic band reconstruction, enabling nonvolatile reversal of the magnon thermal Hall effect while producing anisotropic orbital Hall responses and distinct magneto-optical spectra as complementary transport and optical fingerprints. Our findings establish ferroelasticity as an effective route to nonvolatile magnon control and multichannel state identification in zero net magnetization systems.

papers.title: Intertwined complex orbital order and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb molybdate Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$
papers.authors: Hong-Hao Song, Gang v. Chen
papers.summary_en: The authors study intertwined orbital ordering and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb Fe2Mo3O8.
papers.summary: The authors study intertwined orbital ordering and ferrimagnetism in honeycomb Fe2Mo3O8.
papers.abstract: Motivated by the recent experimental interest in honeycomb molybdates A$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, we return and develop the minimal models to capture the essential physics for Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$. It is pointed out that, the magnetism in these materials arises from the mutual induction between the spin-orbit coupling of the tetrahedral sublattice with active orbitals and the superexchange with the spins from the octahedral sublattice. Essentially, the superexchange between the tetrahedral and octahedral sublattices directly drives the ferrimagnetism, and the residual spin-orbit coupling on the tetrahedral sublattice induces the complex orbital order. The hybrid magnon-phonon excitations are further explored together with their resulting Berry curvatures and thermal Hall effect. We discuss the experimental relevance with Fe$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$, and the framework can be extended to FeNiMo$_3$O$_8$, Ni$_2$Mo$_3$O$_8$ and other isostructural magnets.

papers.title: Vacancy-driven topological transition of a Chern insulator
papers.authors: Peize Ding, Raquel Queiroz
papers.summary_en: Hybridization of vacancy-bound ring states provides a microscopic account of strong-disorder Chern-insulator transitions.
papers.summary: Hybridization of vacancy-bound ring states provides a microscopic account of strong-disorder Chern-insulator transitions.
papers.abstract: We develop a microscopic description of the strong-disorder transition in a Chern insulator using the in-gap ring states bound to individual vacancies. Using Green's function formalism, we construct an energy-dependent Hamiltonian describing their hybridization. In a commensurate periodic vacancy lattice, a Dirac inversion of the zero-energy vacancy kernel accounts for the change in the occupied-state Chern number of the full system. We treat weak positional disorder using the self-consistent Born approximation and numerical disorder averaging, and study independently distributed vacancies using transfer-matrix and multifractal scaling. The local Chern marker and current textures track the transition in real space. Together, these results highlight the role that nonperturbative ring states have as microscopic degrees of freedom through which strong disorder destroys the Chern phase.
